statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low) with no Nasdaq-100 price path available during the CME weekend halt.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published around the 22:00Z CME reopen (00:00 Berlin on 5 October), where the forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on gap and discontinuity risk.
headline: Nasdaq-100 at a record close into the weekend futures halt, with an unresolved Saudi escalation framing the Sunday reopen
body: CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor. The last observed path was orderly: the index traded to an all-time intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday, fully retraced it, and finished at a record 30,807.93 close in the lower quarter of the session range, with VIX settling at 15.31, down 6.59%. Friday's rally followed September payrolls at +29,000 against a +90,000 forecast, which cut rate-hike expectations, while semiconductors led and breadth was broad. Stress is high rather than low because the macro backdrop is unusually tense for a record close: Brent settled at 102.25 and WTI at 91.11, the 10-year note yield closed near 5.28%, and the Saudi-Houthi conflict escalated after the close. The Houthis claimed a ballistic-missile and drone strike on an Aramco refinery south of Riyadh on 3 October, Yemeni government forces struck Sanaa and Saada in response, and neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco have confirmed the cause of the fire or any impact on production, refining or exports. The G7 commitment to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel is an active offsetting supply response. Event importance of this kind informs Stress and Confidence; it does not by itself establish the persistent no-retracement path that Tail measures. The published forecast therefore holds Tail low through the closed Sunday session and raises it into the WATCH band only across the reopen hours, where gap and discontinuity risk is genuine but not yet observable.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours Claude published Tail between 8% and 3%, easing to a 3% floor from 12:00Z on 3 October and holding there, while Stress fell to 52% in the European afternoon and then rebuilt steadily to 73-75% through the weekend halt. Confidence stayed in the 83-88% band. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green, and the dominant mode was normal throughout.
outlookSummary: The closed Sunday session carries no scoreable structure, so Tail is held at 3-8% through 21:00Z with Stress rebuilding from 72% to 79% as unpriced weekend headline flow accumulates. Tail is raised to 21-23%, inside the WATCH band, for the 22:00Z CME reopen and the two hours after it, which form the published danger window. It then decays conditionally to 12% by 04:00Z on the assumption that price discovery is orderly, an assumption that NQ holding a session extreme without meaningful retracement would invalidate. Confidence troughs at 77% late in the halt and peaks at 86% once a live path is observable again.

forecast.analysis: No Nasdaq-100 price path exists this hour: CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z. The last observed path was orderly two-way discovery, with Friday's all-time intraday high of 31,017.53 fully retraced into a record 30,807.93 close sitting in the lower quarter of the session range.

Friday's 31,017.53 intraday record fully retraced into a lower-quarter close
VIX settled 15.31, down 6.59%, confirming volatility decay into the halt
Houthi Aramco claim unconfirmed by Saudi authorities; no supply impact reported

forecast.analysis: Futures stay shut through the European pre-dawn, so Tail cannot be established from structure. Carried risk is headline accumulation: the Houthi claim on the Riyadh refinery is still uncorroborated by Aramco, and any confirmation of damage during this hour would be read at the 22:00Z reopen rather than priced now.

Aramco silence on refinery damage is the open question of the weekend
Any Saudi statement here would price only at the 22:00Z reopen

forecast.analysis: Still a closed tape. Stress eases marginally as Friday's volatility decay remains the most recent market fact, while Confidence begins to erode purely because the Friday 21:00Z reference set ages without any refreshing price observation.
drivers: Friday 21:00Z reference prints are the newest available market evidence
Confidence decays on evidence age, not on any new conflicting signal
No mean-reversion failure is possible while the venue is closed

forecast.analysis: Gulf business hours begin inside this hour, which is the first realistic window for an Aramco or Saudi energy-ministry statement on the Riyadh fire. Scores stay flat because any such statement would be a text event against a halted tape, not observable price structure.
drivers: Gulf business hours open the first realistic Saudi statement window
A confirmed refining outage would lift reopen gap risk, not current Tail
Brent settled 102.25 and WTI 91.11 on Friday, already carrying a risk premium

forecast.analysis: Sunday mid-morning in Europe with no cash or futures venue open. The countervailing fact to the escalation remains the G7 decision to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel, a supply response that argues against treating the weekend headlines as a one-way energy shock.
drivers: G7 pledge of up to 100 million barrels caps the oil-shock interpretation
A frontloaded diesel release lands within the first 20 days
No venue is open, so this hour contributes no directional evidence

forecast.analysis: Conditions are unchanged and unobservable. The relevant distinction for this hour is that the Saudi infrastructure story is already weeks old: the cross-country pipeline was reported back above 80% capacity after earlier attack damage, so the market has repeatedly absorbed this class of headline without a persistent equity trend.
drivers: Saudi cross-country pipeline reported back above 80% of capacity
Repeated absorption of Gulf supply headlines argues against a Tail regime
Stress stays high on the unresolved conflict rather than on price action

forecast.analysis: The quietest point of the weekend window. Confidence reaches its low here because the Friday evidence set is now more than half a day old with no replacement, while Tail stays minimal since a halted market cannot deny mean reversion.
drivers: Evidence age, not evidence conflict, drives the Confidence trough
Tail floor reflects structural impossibility of a path during the halt
Next genuine observation is not available before the 22:00Z reopen

forecast.analysis: Stress begins to rebuild from this hour as the reopen moves inside a ten-hour horizon and weekend positioning risk becomes the dominant consideration. Tail is held at its floor because gap risk is a reopen-hour property and nothing about Sunday afternoon can be observed as structure.
drivers: Reopen moves inside a ten-hour horizon, rebuilding Stress
Gap risk belongs to the 22:00Z slot, not to this hour
Middle East afternoon is the live headline window for the day

forecast.analysis: A first small Tail increment is carried here, reflecting only the shortening distance to the reopen rather than any observed behaviour. If Saudi Arabia proceeds with the reported offensive against the Houthis, that would be a new escalation leg to price at 22:00Z rather than a developing path now.
drivers: Reported Saudi offensive plans against the Houthis are an unresolved leg
Tail increment reflects proximity to the reopen, not observed structure

forecast.analysis: Stress firms as the session approaches. The underlying tension to resolve at the reopen is a genuine cross-asset divergence: Nasdaq-100 at a record close against Brent above 100, the 10-year near 5.28% and VIX at 15.31, which is a complacent volatility price for that macro backdrop.
drivers: Record NQ close against Brent above 100 and the 10-year near 5.28%
VIX at 15.31 prices little of the standing geopolitical risk
Divergence informs Stress and Confidence, not current Tail

drivers: ISM Services (September) at 14:00Z Monday is the first scheduled catalyst

forecast.analysis: Tail steps up modestly as the final pre-reopen stretch begins. The step is a gap-risk allowance only. Whether it is justified will be decided by the opening auction, since the strategy-relevant question is retracement behaviour after the gap print, not the size of the gap itself.
drivers: Final pre-reopen stretch begins; allowance is for gap risk only
Retracement behaviour after the gap, not gap size, decides Tail
No observed structure supports a blocking Tail level at this point

Evidence base is a Friday snapshot plus unconfirmed weekend reporting

forecast.analysis: Tail continues a measured climb toward the reopen window. The asymmetry worth naming for this hour is that an Aramco statement confirming no material damage would compress the entire reopen premium, while continued silence leaves the premium intact into the auction.
drivers: Aramco confirming no material damage would compress the reopen premium
Continued official silence leaves that premium intact into the auction
Climb in Tail is anticipatory and remains well below the block threshold

Mixed mode reflects unresolved cross-asset tension, not observed trend

forecast.analysis: Tokyo joins and liquidity deepens, which historically improves two-way behaviour and makes a persistent one-way path harder to sustain. Tail eases slightly on that liquidity effect while the danger window remains open through the end of this hour.
